lessons.title: Intro
lessons.interactiveContent: What if we wanted our function to make a decision, like adding shipping cost or not, but based on if the cart has a certain value or not?

lessons.title: Intro 2
lessons.interactiveContent: Let's take a look at how to reuse conditionals with functions.

lessons.title: Nesting
lessons.interactiveContent:
When coding a conditional inside the code block of a function like add_shipping, we say that we nest it inside the function.

Make sure to pick add_shipping, followed by if.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Coding a conditional inside a function is called nesting it inside the function.

Define add_shipping and start its nested conditional.

Make sure to pick add_shipping, followed by if.

lessons.title: The function's code block
lessons.interactiveContent:
To nest a conditional like if cart < 100:, we indent it two spaces away from the beginning of the function.

Make sure to pick if, followed by cart < 100, and finally :.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To nest a conditional inside a function, indent it two spaces from the beginning of the function.

Start a conditional that checks whether cart is below 100.

Make sure to pick if, followed by cart < 100, and finally :.

lessons.title: The conditional's code block
lessons.interactiveContent:
Next, we indent the conditional's code block with two spaces, like here with print().

Make sure to pick print followed by ( and then f"Total: {cart + 10}", ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
Indent the conditional's code block another two spaces from the conditional.

Display Total: followed by the cart value plus 10 shipping, using an f-string.

Make sure to pick print, followed by (, f"Total: {cart + 10}", and finally ).

lessons.title: Parameter
lessons.interactiveContent:
To make a conditional work more flexibly, we can use the function's parameter, like cart, as part of the condition.

Make sure to pick cart, followed by cart.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To make a conditional work more flexibly, we can use the function's parameter as part of the condition.

Use the same parameter in the function header and condition so calling with 80 prints Total: 90.

Make sure to pick cart, followed by cart.

lessons.title: The parameter's value
lessons.interactiveContent:
When using the parameter in the condition, we're using the value we pass when calling the function, like 80 here.

Make sure to type 80.

lessons.title: Question: Nesting
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does nesting a conditional inside a function mean?

Indenting the conditional so that it's part of the function's code blockCoding the conditional with the same indentation as the function

Indenting the conditional so that it's part of the function's code block.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Nesting a conditional inside a function means indenting it so it becomes part of the function's code block.

A conditional runs even when its function is never called. Which change places it inside the function?

Indent the conditional under the function definition.Keep the conditional aligned with the function definition.Rename the conditional to match the function.

Indent the conditional under the function definition.

lessons.title: Question: The function's code block
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we indent the conditional in order to nest it in the function's code block?

Two spaces away from the beginning of the functionWe can't indent it

Two spaces away from the beginning of the function.
lessons.hardModeContent:
To nest a conditional in a function, we indent it two spaces from the beginning of the function.

A developer aligns if score > 10: with def check(score):. How should the if line move?

Move it two spaces to the right.Leave it in the same column as def.Move it to the left of the def line.

Move it two spaces to the right.

lessons.title: Question: Parameter
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we use a function's parameter as part of the condition?

Our code can make a decision based on different input valuesWe can't use the function's parameter as part of the condition

Our code can make a decision based on different input values.
lessons.hardModeContent:
When we use a function's parameter as part of the condition, our code can make a decision based on different input values.

Why can can_enter(12) and can_enter(20) take different branches?

The parameter receives each argument, and the condition checks that value.They cannot, because using the same condition always takes the same branch.A parameter keeps only the first argument it ever receives.

The parameter receives each argument, and the condition checks that value.

lessons.title: Question: The parameter's value
lessons.interactiveContent:
What values are the if statement's condition comparing in the example below?

It compares 19 for age with 18It compares a random age value with 18

It compares 19 for age with 18.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The code below calls can_drive(19) and prints Yes they can!.

What would it display if the last line were can_drive(17) instead?

Nothing, because 17 >= 18 is False.Yes they can!, because the condition always uses 19.None, because the function has no return statement.

Nothing, because 17 >= 18 is False.

lessons.title: Example: Nesting
lessons.interactiveContent:
Nest this if-statement that checks if a person can drive inside the can_drive() function.

Make sure to pick if followed by age and then >=, 18, :.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Nest a check that a person is at least 18, so calling with 20 prints Yes they can!.

Make sure to pick if, followed by age, >=, 18, and finally :.

lessons.title: Example: The function's code block
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code an if statement that checks if level <= 20 two spaces away from the beginning of the function.

Make sure to type if level <= 20.

lessons.title: Example: The conditional's code block
lessons.interactiveContent:
Display a message inside the if statement by indenting the print() statement two spaces away from it.

Make sure to pick print followed by ( and then "Low battery!", ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
Inside the if, warn the user, so calling with a low level prints Low battery!.

Make sure to pick print, followed by (, "Low battery!", and finally ).

lessons.title: Example: Parameter
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code a condition that uses > to check if the parameter signups is more than 200.

Make sure to type if signups > 200.

lessons.title: Example: The parameter's value
lessons.interactiveContent:
Call the function with a value so that the if statement's code doesn't run.

Make sure to pick 100.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Choose values so the first call prints nothing and the second prints Waiting list: 20.

Make sure to pick 100, followed by 220.

lessons.title: Nesting else
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can nest all kinds of conditionals inside functions, like this else statement.

Make sure to type else.

lessons.title: Nesting elif
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also nest elif statements, like this one that checks if the operator equals "-".

Make sure to pick elif, followed by operator == "-", and finally :.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can also nest elif statements inside functions.

Add a branch for the minus operator so the call prints 20.

Make sure to pick elif, followed by ==, and finally "-".

lessons.title: Skipping conditionals
lessons.interactiveContent:
Even if the conditional is skipped, the remaining code in the function's code block runs, like the last print().

Make sure to pick print followed by ( and then "Ready for the next level?", ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
After the if, add the line that always runs. With 900 points the branch is skipped, so only Ready for the next level? prints.

Make sure to pick print, followed by (, "Ready for the next level?", and finally ).

lessons.title: Question: Nesting else
lessons.interactiveContent:
How do we indent an else statement when nesting it inside a function?

The same as the if statement, by two spacesThe same as the function, without any spaces

The same as the if statement, by two spaces.
lessons.hardModeContent:
An else nested inside a function uses the same two-space indentation as its if.

A developer places else: with no spaces before it. Which change fixes the nesting?

Indent else: two spaces so it aligns with if.Indent else: four spaces so it aligns with the if body.Leave else: aligned with the function definition.

Indent else: two spaces so it aligns with if.

lessons.title: Question: Nesting elif
lessons.interactiveContent:
What kind of conditionals can we nest inside a function?

if, elif, and else statementsOnly if and else statements

if, elif, and else statements.
lessons.hardModeContent:
We can nest if, elif, and else statements inside a function.

A shipping function needs separate outcomes for low, medium, and high order totals. Which structure fits?

An if branch, an elif branch, and an else branchOnly an if branch and an else branchAn if branch followed by two else branches

An if branch, an elif branch, and an else branch.

lessons.title: Question: Skipping conditionals
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does this display in the console?

You have new messages!Inbox full!

You have new messages!.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If the call changes to show_status(1200), what does the function display?

Inbox full!, followed by You have new messages!Only Inbox full!, because a true if skips the next statementOnly You have new messages!, because the if condition stays false

Inbox full!, followed by You have new messages!

lessons.title: Example: Nesting else
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code an else: statement inside the function.

Make sure to type else:.

Make sure to pick elif followed by score and then ==, 100, :.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Complete one conditional so 20 prints only Score too low and 100 prints only Top score!.

Make sure to pick elif, followed by score == 100, :, "Top score!", and finally 100.

lessons.interactiveContent:
Call the function with a value so that only the last print() statement runs.

Make sure to pick 750.

Print Inbox full! for values above 1000. Choose a call that prints only You have new messages!.
